headline: Sales and margins rise, higher taxes trim the gain
summary_short: Dollar General grew net sales 3.4% y/y to $10.79B in the quarter ended May 1, 2026, with comparable sales up 2.0% and gross margin expanding 65bp to 31.6%; diluted EPS rose to $2.00 from $1.78 a year ago.
summary_long: Net sales rose 3.4% y/y to $10.79B, driven by new-store sales and a 2.0% comp-sales gain (traffic +1.4%, average ticket +0.5%); store closures were a modest offset. Gross margin expanded 65bp to 31.6% on higher markups and lower shrink/damages, partly offset by higher markdowns and transportation costs. SG&A ticked up 25bp of sales on depreciation, utilities and property taxes, partly offset by lower incentive compensation. The effective tax rate rose to 24.9% from 23.4% on expired federal credits. Net income grew 13.3% y/y to $444.1M; diluted EPS was $2.00 versus $1.78. Cash rose to $1.35B; capex guidance for fiscal 2026 remains $1.4-1.5B, funding roughly 450 planned new stores.

drivers.explanation: New-store sales plus same-store sales +2.0% (traffic +1.4%, average ticket +0.5%), partly offset by store closures.
Higher inventory markups and lower shrink/damages drove the gross margin up 65bp to 31.6%, partly offset by increased markdowns and transportation costs.
SG&A rose 25bp of sales on higher depreciation, utilities and property taxes, partly offset by lower incentive compensation; gross-margin gains more than offset this.
Effective tax rate rose to 24.9% from 23.4% on expired federal tax credits, partly offset by lower stock-based compensation expense; interest expense fell $17.4M on lower average borrowings.
Management reiterated plans to open about 450 new stores and complete about 4,730 real estate projects in fiscal 2026, funded within a $1.4-1.5B capex range.
